At 15 and a half, and under 16, a driver who meets the practice, education, and school rules can receive a conditional license after vision and road tests. At 16, a special restricted license is available, and a waiver to drive alone until midnight costs $25. Full privileges come at 17, or after one year on a conditional or special restricted license with no traffic offenses and no at-fault collision. Solo driving on those restricted licenses runs from 6 a.m. to 6 p.m., or 8 p.m. during daylight saving time.

A restricted license is available at 16, and applicants under 18 must have held Stage I for at least six months and passed a road-skills exam. Practice is 50 hours behind the wheel or a state-approved driver education course. Stage II drivers may not drive from midnight to 6 a.m. except in the listed situations, and may not carry more than one passenger other than parents, legal guardians, or family members. An unrestricted license is available at 17, and a 17-year-old must have held Stage II for at least six months.

documents.summary: Identity proof must be a certified original or a certified copy.
documents.quote: The document must be a certified original or a certified copy.

documents.summary: The checklist shows one proof of identity, with a birth certificate or U.S. passport as the example.
documents.quote: Proof of IdentityBirth Certificate or U.S. Passport

documents.summary: Two residency proofs are required for REAL ID. A utility bill or credit card statement is an example.
documents.quote: Utility Bill or Credit Card Statement

documents.summary: The physical Social Security card is not required when a service asks for the number.
documents.quote: Your physical social security card is not required

real_id_summary: As of May 7, 2025, a REAL ID or another federal ID such as a passport may be required to fly within the United States or enter certain federal buildings. The checklist asks for identity, two Oklahoma residency proofs, and the Social Security number.
real_id_quote: As of May 7, 2025, you may need a REAL ID (or a federal ID like a passport) to fly within the U.S.
transfer_summary: A driver license from another state can be transferred without a written or drive test when the driving record meets Service Oklahoma standards and the license is valid or has been expired for no more than six months. The REAL ID checklist lists $42.50 for a new Oklahoma license from another state.
transfer_quote: You can transfer your Driver License from another state without having to take a written or drive test if your driving record meets the standards set by Service Oklahoma
teen_summary: A learner permit is available at 15 while the applicant is in approved driver education and passes the written exam. At 16, driver education is optional. Before an intermediate license, the permit is held at least 180 days, with 50 practice hours including 10 at night, and a Work Zone Safe course is required under 18. With driver education, the intermediate minimum is 16. Without it, the minimum is 16 and a half. Intermediate driving runs from 5 a.m. to 10 p.m. unless the trip is for school, church, or work, or a licensed driver who is at least 21 rides in front. The passenger rule allows one passenger, only household members, or any passengers when that adult is in front. The teen overview lists an unrestricted license at 16 and a half, while the intermediate page requires six months on the intermediate license after driver education or 12 months without it.

teen_points.text: Without driver education, the intermediate license minimum is 16 and a half after 180 days on a learner permit.
teen_points.quote: Must have held a Learner Permit for 180 days and be at least 16 1/2 years old

teen_points.text: With driver education, the intermediate license is held at least six months before an unrestricted license.
teen_points.quote: Must have an Intermediate License for at least 6 months

teen_points.text: Without driver education, the intermediate license is held at least 12 months before an unrestricted license.
teen_points.quote: Must have held an Intermediate License for at least 12 months

teen_points.text: A Work Zone Safe course certificate is required for an intermediate license under 18.
teen_points.quote: WorkZone Safe Course is required to receive an Intermediate License under the age of 18.

out_of_state_permit: An out-of-state learner permit can be transferred if the applicant is at least 15 and a half. Time already held on that permit can count toward the 180-day requirement.
out_of_state_permit_quote: You must be at least 15 1/2 to transfer an Out-of-State Learner Permit
curfew: An intermediate license holder may drive from 5 a.m. to 10 p.m. The limit does not apply for school, church, or work trips, or when a licensed driver who is at least 21 sits in the front seat.
curfew_quote: You can drive from 5:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m.
passengers: An intermediate license holder may drive with one passenger, or only with household members, or with any passengers if a licensed driver who is at least 21 sits in the front seat.
passengers_quote: You can drive with: 1 passengerOR only household members
gaps: The teen driving overview lists an unrestricted license at 16 1/2. The intermediate license page requires six months on that license after driver education, or 12 months without driver education, so some drivers reach unrestricted status later than 16 1/2.
An original learner permit is available at 15. Transferring an out-of-state learner permit requires age 15 1/2. Those are different transactions, so permit_age remains 15.
The drive-test link used here is the Drive Test Center page linked from the teen driving page. That center page was not separately quoted.
